clue.text: Withdraw Conservative member (blue)

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: A Tory MP, feeling glum, backs out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down is an idiom for retreating from a position or backing off a claim.

clue.text: City gutted over Brown — "endless scoffer"

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of City

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Nick Brown, the Labour chief whip of the Blair years

explanation.surface: A sneering remark about a hollowed-out city, aimed at a politician called Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts the first piece above the second in this down clue. Brown is not Gordon but Nick Brown, Labour's chief whip in the Blair years.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic sneers at others' motives, so a scoffer is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Heroin's dodgy when not out at sea

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the adjective/adverb meaning near the shore

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drugs are a risky business unless you're out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore describes waters or vessels close to the coast rather than far out on the open ocean.

clue.text: Halter to restrain tits is an excellent seller

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a blocker is something that halts or stops
slang for breasts, a bust

explanation.surface: A bra-like halter top is a best-selling garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halter' looks like the neck-strap top, but it means a thing that halts something.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a book, film or product that sells in enormous numbers.

clue.text: Too much snow possibly finished parties to a point

parts.note: over means finished, done
dos are parties or celebrations
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: At the end of a party season, someone has had too much cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Snow is slang for cocaine, so too much of it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdose is an excessive, dangerous quantity of a drug such as cocaine.

clue.text: Terrible destructive agent caused by China's infiltration of Vietnam, according to US

indicators.note: one piece infiltrating another means it is put inside it

parts.note: American slang shortens Vietnam to 'Nam
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a pal

explanation.surface: A Cold War account of Chinese infiltration in Vietnam causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is the incendiary jelly dropped by US forces in Vietnam, a horrific weapon.

clue.text: Do everything to ensure each ageing rocker gets the spin treatment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: try every possible means

definitions.text: ensure each ageing rocker gets the spin treatment
definitions.meaning: second meaning: every Rolling Stone is turned over, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: no (Rolling) Stone is left without being turned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to search exhaustively or try every possible avenue.

clue.text: A time to desert the Labour leader in general

indicators.note: to desert is to leave, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: Clement Attlee, post-war Labour leader, spelt here as Atlee, the common misspelling the wordplay needs

explanation.surface: It is time to abandon the Labour leader, in general terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay only works if Attlee is spelt with one T, as it often is; take A and T away and the American Civil War general remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army, the most famous general of that surname.

clue.text: The language when one gets to stuff Bill holding one!

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one
to ram is to stuff or cram

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shoves a bill into something, mid-argument about language.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is the ancient Semitic tongue spoken in Jesus's time.

clue.text: Visually challenged, that's us, as knitting wool is

parts.note: the magazine Private Eye, where this puzzle appears
knitting wool is wound into balls, balled

explanation.surface: The magazine confesses to poor eyesight, its wool all tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visually challenged' looks like a euphemism for poor sight; it means stared down by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eyeballed is to be stared at aggressively, a confrontation through looking.

clue.text: See 6
Piss artist, for instance, backing the House of Lords

parts.note: piss is a crude word for pee
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example, for instance

explanation.surface: A drunkard sponsoring the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss artist is British slang for a drunk, but here the phrase splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the whole body of peers, who sit in the upper chamber of Parliament.

clue.text: Rogue minister runs inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece

parts.note: Robin Cook, Blair's Foreign Secretary
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister gone rogue is running the show from within.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a dishonest person, a villain or scoundrel.

clue.text: Yes, interest lacking in a Daily Mail pisspoor 'key' leader

indicators.note: pisspoor means dreadfully bad, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
A is a musical key
Y is short for yes, as on a Y/N form
I is the abbreviation for interest in finance

explanation.surface: A sneer that the Daily Mail is dull and dreadful, despite its leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' says Y and I leave the letters of A DAILY MAIL; the A from 'key' joins the rest before 'pisspoor' scrambles them. 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial, but it is the Tibetan one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism, so a religious leader.

clue.text: Briefly, penetrating a testicle's agony

parts.note: penetrating means going in
nut is slang for a testicle, with the 's kept
hell means agony or torment

explanation.surface: A wince-making account of a kick in the groin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means put concisely, summed up in few words.

clue.text: Title's definitive foul language has been the undoing of many a featured celeb

definitions.text: has been the undoing of many a featured celeb
definitions.note: a description of the noun phrase, the jinx said to strike those it features

parts.note: the is the definite article
a curse is a swear word
the title is Hello!, the celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A celebrity magazine's swearing has ruined the stars it covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a glossy magazine whose cover couples were famously said to split soon after.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed jinx on stars after a magazine spread is a press legend about broken marriages.

clue.text: Transport politician has nothing on the French phallic symbol

parts.note: to tote is to carry
MP, Member of Parliament
O looks like zero
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A transport minister with nothing on, beside a phallic French symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a tall carved post, often read as phallic in shape.

clue.text: Loveable arsehole, Archer (as called), at heart

indicators.note: at heart means inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer is fondly called a lovable bastard, at least deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and disgraced Tory peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous scamp, a rogue one is fond of.

clue.text: As the sun rises .. always a Sir Robin?

definitions.text: As the sun rises .. always a Sir Robin?

parts.words: As the sun rises .. always a Sir Robin?
parts.note: the sun comes up daily; and the saying 'once a ..., always a ...' applied to Sir Robin Day, the broadcaster

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robin Day was a famous BBC political interviewer; the second half completes the saying 'once a X, always a X'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means daily, every twenty-four hours, which is how often sunrise happens.

clue.text: A hotel in Bristol and Cyclops Island

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang for breasts (Bristol City, titty), so one is a tit
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
the setter Cyclops, who would say I

explanation.surface: A Bristol hotel and the setter, sharing an island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristols is Cockney rhyming slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Went in for bondage, though married?

explanation.definitionFit: Hitched means tied fast to something, and getting hitched is slang for getting wed.

clue.text: See 6
Grunge group in a perfect state

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Kurt Cobain's Seattle band
second meaning: the Buddhist state of perfect bliss

explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist goal of release from suffering, and the name of a 1990s Seattle rock band.

clue.text: What Blair represents: a new Balfour? F-off!

definitions.note: a description of the party Blair led

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Is Blair just a reborn Arthur Balfour? Get lost!
explanation.walkthrough: Balfour was a Conservative prime minister; with its F sent off, the rest is rearranged, a nod to New Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair led the Labour Party, rebranded as New Labour, into government in 1997.

clue.text: Assassinated democrat, centre of 'knoll' procession

indicators.note: assassinated means violently destroyed, so the letters are broken up
the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter of knoll

explanation.surface: Kennedy, the murdered Democrat, and the grassy knoll of Dallas conspiracy lore.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, as at Dallas in 1963.

clue.text: Band Oasis centre on drug experience

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter of Oasis
a trip is a drug-induced experience

explanation.surface: The band Oasis focusing on a drug trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis looks like the band to define; it only supplies a letter, and 'Band' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a long narrow band of material.

clue.text: Stout Party leader upset party getting homosexual one removed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: removed means the letter is taken out

parts.note: gay means homosexual
A means one

explanation.definitionFit: Podgy means chubby or plump, a synonym for stout as an adjective.

clue.text: See 14
Act as cattle brought down

explanation.definitionFit: Cows low, that is moo, and low also means depressed in spirits.

clue.text: Having an erection after Wilt, the film

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other

parts.note: to die is to wilt, as flowers do
hard, erect

explanation.walkthrough: Wilt is also a Tom Sharpe novel and film, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Hard is the 1988 Bruce Willis action movie.

clue.text: Present arse, with love, to wife

parts.note: end is a word for backside
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A crude gesture: mooning at the wife, with love.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or bestow, as with a gift or bequest.

clue.text: Tars collectively e.g. Prince Edward with any vice possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vice, as in VP

explanation.walkthrough: Tars are sailors; Prince Edward famously quit the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is the British fleet and its sailors as a body.
